findings.title: Hardcoded secret credential exposed in source
findings.body:
A hardcoded string `PARTNER_TOKEN` is assigned a value that looks like a credential (`FAKE_TEST_CREDENTIAL_DO_NOT_USE`). This token is used in the authorization check on line 6, so it is effectively a secret. Hardcoded secrets belong in environment variables or a secrets manager, not in source code.

According to custom instructions in 'Error Handling Standards' (Every external call and I/O operation has error handling): this hardcoded value is an I/O-like configuration that should be externalized and handled safely.

findings.title: Authorization function lacks input validation and error handling
findings.body:
The function `can_read_private_records` compares the input `token` directly to the hardcoded secret without validating the input type or handling potential exceptions (e.g., if `token` is not a string). This can lead to unexpected behavior or security issues if the input is malformed or missing.

According to custom instructions in 'Error Handling Standards' (Every external call and I/O operation has error handling): the function performs an external-like comparison without any safeguards or error handling.

findings.title: Authorization logic is inverted and overly permissive
findings.body:
The function returns `True` when the input token matches the hardcoded secret, which is the opposite of a secure default. A secure authorization function should default to denying access unless explicitly permitted. This inversion could allow unintended access if the hardcoded secret is leaked or bypassed.

According to custom instructions in 'Naming Consistency' (A name says what the value is or what the function does): the function name `can_read_private_records` implies a permissive check, but the logic is inverted relative to secure defaults.
findings.suggestion: return token is not None and token == PARTNER_TOKEN

summary.problem: The new authorization module hardcodes a secret credential and implements an inverted, insecure authorization check without input validation or error handling.
summary.done_well: The module is small and focused on a single responsibility. The function name clearly indicates its purpose.
